summary: Pole light of 1887 at the Budd Inlet entrance, replaced by an eight-sided concrete tower in 1934; local caretakers, not a formal keeper; Coast Guard property, closed.

staffing.note: NRHP: automated when the 1934 tower was built; LighthouseFriends: the Coast Guard automated the light in the 1960s

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) Automation: LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard automated the light in the 1960s and the fog signal in 1987; the NRHP (1995) says the light was automated when the 1934 tower was built and the fog horn in 1976. The story states both. (2) Land: LighthouseFriends dates a claim of 316 acres to 27 September 1865; the NRHP says the Dofflemyers located in Thurston County in 1851 or 1852 and took out a '320 Donation Land Claim' at the point. The story gives the NRHP's wording and does not give the acreage as a settled figure. (3) Tower date: LighthouseFriends 1934; NRHP 1933-34 with design 1933 and replacement of the pole light in 1934 or 1935. (4) Range: the record gives 7.0 nm; the NRHP (1995) says 'nine mile range'. (5) Characteristic: the record gives Fl W 4s; the NRHP (1995) describes a 6-second light; the Light List was not accessed. (6) First light: the NRHP describes 'a light suspended on a pole on a wharf at the point', 20 feet above high water; LighthouseFriends describes a lens lantern on a twelve-foot stake set up on 13 December 1887. The story states both descriptions and that they differ. (7) Keepers have no USLHS roster (none listed by roster.py), so no person slugs are given. Sperring's start date is unknown. Nellie Vassell's start date is not given. Madeline Campbell's start is not dated (LighthouseFriends says the 1960s); her service end is 1976 in the NRHP and 1987 (fog signal automation) in LighthouseFriends; the record's 'to: 1976' follows the NRHP. (8) The contractor: the NRHP text (OCR) reads 'Rufuss Kindle'; the form's architect/builder field reads 'Rufus Kindle'. The story uses 'Rufus Kindle'. The NRHP OCR also has 'Alien' for Allen, 'Dofflemyre' as an alternate spelling, and 'hi' for 'in'; the section 8 continuation sheets carry no printed page numbers, so citations are by section. (9) Corpus: no Light-House Board (1891-1901), Lighthouse Service Bulletin (1912-1939) or Commissioner (1915-1922) entry for this light; the 1917 Bulletin entry for Budd Inlet is day marks at Olympia Harbor, not this light. (10) Chronicling America: 20 Washington-paper pages for 'Dofflemyer' 1887-1950 (mostly the Washington Standard, Olympia); the one page read (1912, p. 3) names family members, not the light; the rest were not read. (11) Not read: the Daily Olympian (1937) and Light List entries the NRHP cites; the Coast Guard history site. (12) Record coordinates 47.140515, -122.907261; LighthouseFriends gives 47.14057, -122.90749 (not a correction). (13) The 'designed in 1933 by P.H.P.' designer is not identified; the form's architect/builder field gives 'P.H.P./Rufus Kindle', the text gives Kindle as the local contractor.
